stem:
Farid already knows a rectangle-diagonal construction. He asks what extra diagonal condition turns that construction into a square construction.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call the answer "diagonal" only, without stating any extra square condition on the diagonals.
Say that naming the figure a square is what creates equal diagonals that meet at right angles, instead of using those diagonal conditions to build the square.
Require diagonals that are equal, bisect each other, and meet at right angles (they also bisect the square's angles).
Switch to a circle-and-radius construction for a regular hexagon, and treat that method as this square-diagonal condition.

teacher.key_rationale: A square needs equal diagonals that bisect each other at right angles (and bisect the angles). Naming only "diagonal", reversing name and conditions, or swapping in a hexagon circle construction all leave this hinge.
